definition: Two packages trace to a common upstream carrier or provenance root.
boundary: Does not establish shared access or contact.

definition: Both packages expose values through interfaces with a common declared codomain or vocabulary.
boundary: Matching labels do not establish semantic identity.

definition: A single quotient or jointly audited quotient map is defined on the compared carrier.
boundary: Does not establish strict joint information.

definition: One admissible instrument can interrogate both packages under a common protocol.
boundary: Instrument mediation can itself create exposure and must be priced.

definition: Contact/admission conditions are fixed before the outcome or foreign record is known.
certificate: timestamped immutable rule, budget, and subject binding
boundary: Post-hoc compatibility is not prospective commitment.

definition: A package projects lawfully to both parents.
certificate: two faithful projections and retention audit
boundary: May be a product/fork rather than a strict join.

definition: A formed common refinement carries a distinction that does not factor through either parent or their mere product under the declared comparison.
certificate: objecthood, retention, anti-product witness, source and cost ledger
boundary: Does not by itself establish a P6 arrow or endogenous birth.
